description: A plant manager must decide how to take an overhead crane out of service and organize the week's frame movements after a maintenance concern, with input from maintenance, production scheduling, and environmental health and safety.

shared_context.S1: The 25-ton overhead crane in Bay 2 is used to move fabricated frames between welding, inspection, and shipping.
shared_context.S2: The crane is currently operating, and its routine annual inspection is scheduled for Friday.
shared_context.S3: Eight finished frames are staged in Bay 2, and four additional frames are expected to reach the bay during the week.
shared_context.S4: Mara makes the final decision, and the plant's standard pre-job huddle asks maintenance, production scheduling, and EHS to review the work plan before equipment-service decisions are finalized.

PF1.text: During Jonas's inspection this morning, the crane brake lining measured 18% remaining; the maintenance standard requires immediate removal from service below 20%, a 6-hour brake replacement, and a 125% rated-capacity proof-load test before the crane returns to service. Jonas has not entered the finding in the maintenance system yet.

PF2.text: Priya's confirmed shipping schedule requires exactly 8 frames to be moved to shipping by Thursday at 15:00; the remaining 4 frames may remain in Bay 2 until Monday. She received the confirmation from the customer logistics desk this morning but has not updated the shared production board.

PF3.text: Elliot's EHS walkdown found that the forklift route through Bay 2 crosses the active pedestrian aisle, so forklifts may not substitute for the overhead crane there; any crane work or proof-load test requires a 10-meter exclusion zone and a designated spotter. Elliot recorded the finding in his walkdown notes but has not issued the bay notice.

acceptance_conditions: The overhead crane must be removed from service.
Brake replacement must be scheduled for exactly 6 hours.
A 125% rated-capacity proof-load test must be required before return to service.
Exactly 8 frames must be assigned for movement by Thursday at 15:00.
Forklifts must not be allowed as an alternative lifting method in Bay 2.
A 10-meter exclusion zone and designated spotter must be required.
Maintenance, shipping-movement, and EHS-control commitments must be recorded.
The brake-wear finding must be cited in the decision justification after Jonas states it.

decisive_facts.why: The measured 18% brake lining changes the crane status to removed from service, fixes the repair duration at exactly 6 hours, and requires a 125% proof-load test and brake-replacement commitment.
The confirmed Thursday shipment changes the movement assignment to exactly 8 frames by 15:00 and requires a frame-movement plan commitment.
The blocked forklift route changes the alternative-lift decision to prohibited, fixes the exclusion zone at 10 meters, requires a designated spotter, and requires a bay-exclusion control commitment.
